text:
Alex: heads up — seeing a sustained retry spike and lopsided traffic to a few endpoints for svc/gpu-infer (us-west-2). 5xxs from model-worker pods + kube-proxy conn reuse weirdness. logs attached below.
Priya: can you paste kube-proxy logs and ipvs table? quick glance: symmetric retries -> IPVS suspect.
Alex: logs snippet:
```
I0304 14:02:15.123 kube-proxy: ipvs: forwarding to 10.10.34.11:8080 failed, retries=4, reason=timeout
I0304 14:02:15.124 kube-proxy: established conn: svc 172.20.5.22 -> ep 10.10.34.11 (weight=100)
```
Priya: ran ipvsadm on an affected node — shows heavy persistent connections to two endpoints only:
```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats
TCP  172.20.5.22:8080 rr,timeout=0,masq
  -> 10.10.34.11:8080      Masq    12423      10234567
  -> 10.10.34.12:8080      Masq    45         345678
  -> 10.10.34.13:8080      Masq    3          2345
```
Marco: interesting — rdma nodepool (nodepool-rdma-usw2) had a kernel/net driver bump from the deploy at ~1765430000. I saw MTU mismatch across NICs: some nodes reporting mtu 9000, others 1500. ip link output:
```
2: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
3: ib0: mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 256
```
Marco: RDMA stacks + mixed MTU can produce retransmits and uneven flow hashing at L2 causing conn failovers and IPVS skew.
Jen: we should avoid large topology changes during kernel rollouts. Immediate mitigation options: 1) rotate kube-proxy on the affected nodes to rebuild IPVS tables (cheap, quick) 2) cordon+drain the worst nodes and let scheduler shift pods (slower) 3) fallback routing: temporarily adjust service sessionAffinity or use a small canary weight for problematic endpoints.
ops-oncall: deploy-bot shows a cluster-wide kernel/driver rollout at 1765430000 (can confirm). tagging rollout id: roll/driver-update-2026-03-04.
deploy-bot: rollout(roll/driver-update-2026-03-04) completed stage: nodepool-rdma-usw2 at 1765430023
Alex: quick test from a healthy node -> single pod shows 20% packet loss to ib0 on one of the endpoints:
```
# ping -I ib0 10.10.34.11 -c 10
--- 10.10.34.11 ping statistics ---
10 packets transmitted, 8 received, 20% packet loss, time 9009ms
```
Priya: temp fix I'm pushing now: increase kube-proxy ipvs sync period and restart kube-proxy DaemonSet on nodepool-rdma-usw2 to clear stale conn tables. command:
```
kubectl -n kube-system set env daemonset/kube-proxy KUBE_PROXY_ARGS="--ipvs-sync-period=5s"
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy -n kube-system --selector=nodepool=rdma-usw2
```
Jen: also start cordoning the top 3 high-error nodes and evict GPU pods to avoid wasted GPU cycles. We'll failover to us-east reserved pool if needed (ops-oncall note: extra cross-region traffic will increase egress/costs).
ops-oncall: estimated cost delta if we shift 40% of gpu inference traffic to us-east reserved pool for 2h: ~+$1.8k. Approve? (type :+1: to proceed)
Marco: creating infra ticket INFRA-1728 with logs, ipvsadm output, and kernel rollout id. We'll also mark driver rollback as option if next checks fail.
Alex: after kube-proxy restart, connection distribution improved (counts more even) and retries dropped ~85% in 6 minutes. leaving monitoring on for 30m. thanks all.
Jen: follow-up: schedule a postmortem with driver vendor and plan stricter MTU validation in our rollout playbook. :eyes:
